item.title: Avatar: Seven Havens Officially Recasts Korra’s Voice
item.dc:creator: Willa Rowe
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV/animated series casting news; matches past TOSS pattern.] Avatar: Seven Havens' latest episodes revealed who will be voicing Korra in the series
item.content:encoded: One of the most important characters inAvatar: Seven Havens is Korra, even if she's long dead by the time the show starts. The post-apocalyptic world of Seven Havens is directly caused by Korra's actions; at least that is what the show has indicated so far, resulting in widespread hatred toward the Avatar. This is causing a lot of problems for Nisha and Pavi, our new Avatar twins. The most recent batch of episodes brought us even closer to Korra once again and also revealed who provides her voice in Seven Havens.

item.content:encoded: As a follower of Schoenbrun’s work, I can’t help but know so much about them. I know that they used to work as a film critic before directing and writing movies. I know that they’re trans, and that their work is in constant conversation with that identity. It has propelled them to become one of the most notable voices in indie cinema.

item.title: FBI Is Officially Investigating An Unprecedented Pokémon Card Heist
item.dc:creator: Patricia Hernandez
item.description: [Filtered: Pokémon TCG retail/heist story; matches past TOSS profile.] The disappearance of over 6,450 cards on a FedEx truck might make this the biggest Pokémon TCG theft of all time
item.content:encoded: Earlier in October, authorities revealed that a FedEx truck reportedly containing nearly $1 million in cards graded by the Professional Sports Authenticator had suddenly gone missing. A couple of weeks later, the apparent theft of 6,451 slabs — many of which contained Pokémon cards — is being scrutinized by the Federal Bureau of Investigation.

item.title: 27 Years Ago, 'Buffy the Vampire' Unleashed an Impossibly Good Season, and Broke the Fandom
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show, despite horror tag.] Buffy Season 3 is the best Halloween binge watch with thrilling villains and unforgettable moments.
item.content:encoded: Buffy the Vampire Slayer was no exception. The show's first season was mixed at best, as the cast and writers all struggled to find their footing. Yet Buffy season 2 easily has one of the finest batches of episodes in television history, largely thanks to the introduction of iconic vampire baddies Spike (James Marsters) and Druscilla (Juliet Landau), along with Angel's (David Boreanaz) transformation into the villainous bloodsucker Angelus.

item.title: Amazon's Fourth Wing Show Reportedly Set to Start Filming Soon
item.dc:creator: Ashely Claudino
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV adaptation news without substantial prestige credentials.] Reports reveal the filming window and location for the Fourth Wing show, indicating it's nearly ready to move out of pre-production.
item.content:encoded: Fourth Wing went viral on BookTok in 2023, amassing fans all over the world. These thousands of avid readers are anticipating Amazon's adaptation of their favorite romantasy series. As more details come out, it's clear that it is close to leaving pre-production. Recent reports provide details about its filming window and location, allowing fans to speculate about the real-world location that will become Navarre and Basgiath War College.

item.title: 10 Best 'Star Trek: Original Series' Episodes of All Time, Ranked
item.dc:creator: Terry Terrones
item.description: [Filtered: Generic TV retrospective ranking list without substance.] From iconic villains to heartbreaking sacrifices, these 10 episodes show why the original Star Trek remains essential television.
item.content:encoded: Ask 10 Star Trek fans to name the best episodes from The Original Series , and you're likely to get 10 completely different lists. Some will prioritize the writing, others the performances or the science-fiction concepts. And inevitably, somebody will argue that "The City on the Edge of Forever" belongs at No. 1. They might even be right.

item.title: 27 Years Later, the Best Action Adventure Movie of 1999 Is Officially Free on Youtube
item.dc:creator: Maria Loreto
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Brendan Fraser’s best ‘90s blockbuster had a secret ingredient two reboots couldn’t copy
item.content:encoded: No one really knows why a movie works. After a century of Hollywood, the industry is still trying to understand and adapt to an ever-evolving audience. As we enter an era of peak remake and IP-grab filmmaking, stories from decades ago have become the studios’ easiest bets to make money. It’s not fertile ground for creativity, but we movie fans have to take our wins where we can.

item.title: Sydney Sweeney's New Netflix Sci-Fi Space Epic Gets First Details
item.description: [Filtered: Big-franchise churn: Gundam anime adaptation casting gossip.] Netflix's live-action Gundam adaptation stars Sydney Sweeney and Noah Centineo in a Shakespearian action romance space movie epic.
item.content:encoded: The live-action Gundam film has been in the works in some form or another since 2018. A director and cast have been announced, including high-profile names like Sydney Sweeney joining the project. Still, hard details on exactly what Netflix's live-action adaptation of the legendary mech anime series will look like have been almost non-existent.

item.title: 15 Years Later, Batman: Arkham City Remains Batman's Last Gaming Masterpiece
item.dc:creator: Austin Manchester
item.category: LEGO Batman: Legacy of the Dark Knight
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old game from 15 years ago.] Batman: Arkham City set a new highwater mark for superhero games and has influenced their design and mechanics in the 15 years since its release.
item.content:encoded: Batman: Arkham Asylum was released in 2009 at a time when superhero video games were usually relegated to being uninspired movie tie-ins. Some of them were good, like X-Men Origins: Wolverine, but most of them were either forgettable or downright bad. Arkham Asylum was something different — a superhero game based on an original idea from a renowned Batman writer, Paul Dini (Batman: The Animated Series). It was great, and set the foundation for its even greater 2011 follow-up.

item.title: 6 Hilarious 'Calvin and Hobbes' Comics Where Calvin is a Weird Little Genius
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Generic comics/graphic novel excerpt; not gaming or horror.] Words and verbs and adjectives, painted up like a picture in these iconic Calvin and Hobbes comic strips
item.content:encoded: Calvin and Hobbes came along at just the right time to influence a generation of creators, many of whom would go on to create comic strips of their own. Alongside a couple of other seminal '90s newspaper comics like Bloom County/Outland, C&H's linework, flexibility, and imagination visibly inspired many of the artists who worked in the 2000s webcomics boom.

item.title: Clayface Gives Skydance Its Second Box Office Weekend Win In A Row
item.dc:creator: Tomas Franzese
item.description: [Filtered: DC franchise box office churn; not prestige/genuinely anticipated] Clayface held off You Can See Everything to top the box office this weekend
item.content:encoded: Initial estimates for Clayface's opening weekend box office are in, and the lower-budget horror film took the top spot with a $24.5 million gross. Its success means Skydance, the company created when Paramount and Warner Bros. merged, has topped the box office for two straight weeks.

item.title: GTA: San Andreas’ Most Frustrating MIssion Show How Far Rockstar Has Come in 22 Years
item.dc:creator: Paulo Kawanishi
item.category: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas – The Definitive Edition
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old game from 22 years ago] Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas is a classic game with interesting missions, but its annoying controls just feel worse after 22 years.
item.content:encoded: With the imminent release of Grand Theft Auto 6, I decided it was time to revisit what was probably the biggest game of my childhood: Grand Theft Auto: San Andreas. In 2005, GTA: San Andreas was one of the first four games I bought for the PlayStation 2, alongside Final Fantasy X, Kingdom Hearts, and Devil May Cry 3. Since I can no longer enjoy that version of the game I played so many times as a kid, I picked up the Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy — Definitive Edition, which includes San Andreas, on Steam and booted up the game.

item.title: 9 Near-Perfect 'Far Side' Comics Starring the Nerdy Kid
item.dc:creator: Brian VanHooker
item.description: [Filtered: Comic retrospective, not games or Steven's stated interests.] Gary Larson's The Far Side didn't really have recurring characters, though some faces did appear more than once, like the Nerdy Kid
item.content:encoded: One of the biggest differences between The Far Side and most other comic strips is that The Far Side doesn’t have a recurring cast of characters. Charles Schulz’s Peanuts, for example, had Charlie Brown, Linus, Lucy, Snoopy, and the rest of the gang, while Jim Davis’ Garfield has Garfield, Odie, Jon, and a handful of other recurring characters. But Gary Larson’s The Far Side, with its non-sequitur, single-panel jokes, didn’t have regular characters, or at least not really.

item.title: 5 Near-Perfect Psychological Thriller Movies Streaming for Free
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] These tense genre picks are well worth your time.
item.content:encoded: Psychological thrillers trigger a fight-or-flight response within a controlled environment and entertain us at the same time. Interpersonal relationships become the source of anxiety, as there’s more at stake than someone’s physical safety — their very sanity is on the line. The novelty of great psychological thrillers like Rear Window (1954), Memento (2000), or Mulholland Drive (2001) does not wear off after a first watch. There’s more to glean than suspense or twist, as catharsis is an integral part of the experience. Unfortunately, all those movies are locked up behind various streaming service subscriptions (if they're available to stream at all).

item.title: 23 Years Later, Spike's Best 'Buffy' Quote Is Still One of the Best Lines in TV History
item.dc:creator: Jake Kleinman
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show, not new content.] Spike's best quote sums up his arc as one of the main characters in Buffy the Vampire Slayer.
item.content:encoded: Buffy’s writers gave Spike some of the show’s sharpest one-liners — who could forget “Out. For. A. Walk. Bitch.”? But his best line comes in the series finale, “Chosen.” It’s the natural culmination of a character pulled between heroism and selfishness for most of his life, and it captures the complicated truth of his relationship with Buffy.

item.title: 61 Years Later, Paul's Best Dune Line Is Still the Coldest Quote in Sci-Fi History
item.dc:creator: Debopriyaa Dutta
item.description: [Filtered: Book quote retrospective, not games or horror content.] This brilliant quote from Frank Herbert's Dune reveals an unsavory truth.
item.content:encoded: That said, the phenomenal success of Denis Villeneuve’s Dune movies proves that the impossible is always within reach. So far, Villeneuve’s adaptation has captured the sheer scale of the books and also made some meaningful changes to the source material. This version of Paul Atreides (Timothée Chalamet) begins his journey with a hesitant vulnerability that feels more intense than in the books. This is also why his turn as a self-proclaimed messiah feels more ominous and devastating in Dune: Part Two.

item.title: Forget Tom Cruise, Sci-Fi's Foundational 1950s Classic Movie Is Free to Watch on YouTube
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Every little green man from space for 70 years owes his existence to this flick from 1953
item.content:encoded: H.G. Wells' The War of the Worlds is a punchline now, and it's Amazon's fault. At time of writing, the newest adaptation of The War of the Worlds is a "screenlife" movie from 2025 that’s a frontrunner for the worst film of the 21st century.

item.title: 58 Years Later, Captain Kirk's Best Star Trek Quote Is the Greatest Line in Sci-Fi History
item.dc:creator: Terry Terrones
item.description: [Filtered: Nostalgia retrospective about old TV show quotes.] Captain Kirk's speech in 'Return to Tomorrow' says more about what Star Trek stands for than any other line in the original series.
item.content:encoded: Certain lines of dialogue become so famous they almost stop belonging to the movies and TV shows that produced them. “May the Force be with you.” “I’ll be back.” “You're gonna need a bigger boat.” You don't need to know the context. The words have long since transcended their original context.

item.title: Jean-Claude Van Damme's First Action Classic is Streaming for Free
item.dc:creator: Thomas Hindmarch
item.description: [Filtered: Rule: streaming clickbait headline] Forged by fire, a beast in the night
item.content:encoded: Jean-Claude Van Damme gets a bad rap. Due to when he got famous and the sorts of movies that he usually makes, JCVD often gets lumped in with other B-tier '80s action stars like Steven Seagal and Chuck Norris, which does Van Damme a disservice.
